clauses.reason: Section 1 establishes the Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal, with ribbons and appurtenances, for award by the Secretary of Defense or, for the Coast Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy, by a second Cabinet secretary, and makes Armed Forces members who perform outstanding volunteer service eligible. No end date, condition or sunset appears in this clause and no held instrument ends it. It is operative on 2026-10-14. Record read for context, not used as the registered basis because its bytes are held only by hash: Order printed in the U.S. Code as a note preceding 10 U.S.C. 1121 (title 10, subtitle A, part II, chapter 57 note), as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 13286 sec. 28; U.S. Code release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09; no revocation or end noted. Executive Order 13286 section 28 (effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92) struck the words naming the Secretary of Transportation wherever they appear and inserted the Secretary of Homeland Security; before: the Coast Guard award authority sat with the Secretary of Transportation; after: it sits with the Secretary of Homeland Security. Under the strike-and-insert ruling the clause continues, amended.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 12830 (58 FR 4061, January 13, 1993) establishes the Military Outstanding Volunteer Service Medal. The held Federal Register text was read in full; the four sections are separate commands with no end date, condition or sunset. The only held later instrument is Executive Order 13286 section 28, which substituted the Secretary of Homeland Security for the Secretary of Transportation in Sections 1 and 4. The U.S. Code (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09) still prints the order as amended. The three bounded searches found no revocation, supersession or expiry. The order is therefore claimed as in force on 2026-10-14. The original is the Federal Register text layer; its page images were not separately re-read.
Earlier end: Earlier-end test: the only held later instrument naming this order is Executive Order 13286 section 28, an amendment; the Office of the Federal Register note on this order reads 'Amended by: EO 13286, February 28, 2003' and records no revocation. Chain entries in the dossier that name Executive Order 12977 repeat the same section 28 wording under that order's label; Executive Order 12977 itself does not cite this order (the number search of held texts found six citing texts, all Executive Order 13286 copies).
Current basis: Current predicate: the U.S. Code note printing this order 'as amended by Ex. Ord. No. 13286, § 28' is held (release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09), and the bounded searches current-law:usc (2 hits, the note and the 13286 note), current-law:ecfr (0 hits) and later-events:ofr_catalog (1 hit, the amendment) found no ending.
